corrected_value.title: A genome-wide association study reveals ARL15, a novel non-HLA susceptibility gene for rheumatoid arthritis in North Indians
corrected_value.authors: Negi S, Juyal G, Senapati S, Prasad P, Gupta A, Singh S, et al.

decisions.quote: Some Indian population-specific studies were done to find an association between non-HLA gene  PTPN22  polymorphisms and RA but found no significant association,[ 11 , 12 ] but  ARL15  variant rs255758 was found to be significantly associated with north Indian population-specific genome-wide association study (GWAS).[ 13 ] The link between homozygous variant genotype ( CC ) in  ARL15  intronic SNP rs255758 and RA patients was supported by this study.[ 13 ]
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding (target 0) correctly identify Reference 13 (Negi et al., 2013, doi: 10.1002/art.38110) as the original study whose reported association between ARL15 variant rs255758 (and its homozygous CC genotype) and rheumatoid arthritis in North Indians is re-tested by this replication study. Reference 15 (Pandey et al., 2021) examined ARL15 protein levels, which are not measured here, and Reference 27 (Wang et al., 2017) is discussed only as a cross-population comparison in the Discussion.

decisions.quote: Results from the present study are found to be analogous to the earlier study done on the north Indian population[ 13 ] and showed the statistical significance of  ARL15  polymorphism rs255758 with RA in the northwest Indian population ( P  = 0.024).
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding correctly classify the replication outcome for Negi et al. (2013) [13] as 'successful'. The authors explicitly report that their results are analogous to the earlier North Indian study [13], finding a statistically significant association of ARL15 rs255758 with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.024, risk allele C, and OR = 2.54, P = 0.004 under the recessive CC vs. CA+AA model) and concluding that the study corroborates and replicates the earlier Indian population findings.

decisions.quote: The objective of the present study was to perform a replication case–control-based association study of variant rs255758, to determine its association with RA, in an independent cohort from the population of northwest India.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding correctly classify the study type as 'replication'. The authors collected new blood samples and genotyped an independent cohort of 188 rheumatoid arthritis cases and 310 healthy controls from northwest India to re-test the previously published association of ARL15 variant rs255758 with rheumatoid arthritis.
